title: Android apps
description: For an Android app in Kotlin or Java: Play target API level, exported components, cleartext traffic, runtime permissions, release optimization and lint.

sources.title: Android Developers, meet Google Play's target API level requirement
Android Developers, improve your code with lint checks

rules.instruction: Set `targetSdk` to the API level Google Play requires for new apps and updates, and review the behavior changes of each level crossed.
rules.verification: Compare `targetSdk` in the app module's Gradle file with the current requirement on the Play target API page, and run the instrumented tests on that API level.

rules.instruction: Set `android:exported` explicitly on every activity, service, receiver and provider, and export only components other apps must start.
rules.verification: Review the merged manifest of the release build for components without `android:exported` or exported without a reason.

rules.instruction: Keep cleartext traffic disabled. Allow it only for named domains in the network security configuration, never in `base-config` of a release build.
rules.verification: Inspect `network_security_config.xml` and the merged manifest for `cleartextTrafficPermitted="true"` and `usesCleartextTraffic`.

rules.instruction: Request each dangerous permission when the user starts the feature that needs it, and keep the app usable when the user denies it.
rules.verification: Deny each new permission on a test device, run the feature, and confirm the app explains what is unavailable without crashing or blocking.

rules.instruction: Enable R8 code and resource optimization for the release build type, with keep rules for code reached by reflection.
rules.verification: Build the release variant and run the smoke tests on that build, not only on the debug build.

rules.instruction: Run Android lint on the changed modules and fix new errors, or record them in the lint baseline with a reason.
rules.verification: Run `./gradlew lint` in CI and check that the report shows no new error compared with the baseline.
